rationale: Across clinical reviews and cohorts characterizing Loeys-Dietz syndrome (LDS) subtypes, significant primary intellectual disability is documented as exceedingly rare in SMAD2-associated LDS (LDS6), where cognitive development is typically normal or limited to mild speech delays secondary to hypotonia or motor hypermobility rather than true intellectual disability. Furthermore, later-identified LDS genotypes including SMAD2 (LDS6) exhibit notably lower frequencies of severe craniofacial features such as frank craniosynostosis compared to classic severe LDS1/2 (TGFBR1/2) or Shprintzen-Goldberg syndrome (SKI). The presence of prominent craniosynostosis combined with significant intellectual disability specifically suggests alternate diagnoses such as Shprintzen-Goldberg syndrome rather than typical SMAD2 LDS6.

evidence.text: Later-identified LDS genes such as TGFB2, TGFB3, and SMAD2 (LDS4, 5, 6) exhibit notably lower severity and penetrance of classic severe features, and speech delays in LDS typically relate to hypotonia and hypermobility rather than primary cognitive deficiency.
